title: Derived self-tensor for a flat surjection
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings such that $B$ is flat as an $A$-module. Then the canonical multiplication morphism $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\to B[0]$ is an isomorphism in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 08R2 (lemma-when-zero), cases (1)--(2): a flat epimorphism is a special case of the flat diagonal case; the derived tensor is represented by the ordinary tensor under flatness

proof.text: Put $f:A\to B$ for the given surjection and regard $B$ as an $A$-module through $f$. For any acyclic $A$-module complex $F^\bullet$, each sequence $F^{n-1}\to F^n\to F^{n+1}$ is exact. Since $B$ is flat, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] says that $F^{n-1}\otimes_A B\to F^n\otimes_A B\to F^{n+1}\otimes_A B$ is exact for every $n$. The total tensor with $B[0]$ is precisely this termwise tensor complex, so it is acyclic. Thus $B[0]$ is K-flat by [def-pc-module-kflat-complex].

Apply clause (2) of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with its base ring $R=A$, target ring $A=B$, second complex $N=B[0]$, and first complex $E=B[0]$. By Step 1 the identity $B[0]\to B[0]$ is a K-flat resolution. The resulting canonical K-flat computation identifies $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ with $(B\otimes_A B)[0]$ in $D(B)$, with the $B$-action through the second factor. In this identity-resolution model the canonical derived multiplication is represented by the ordinary multiplication chain map $\mu[0]$, where $\mu(b\otimes c)=bc$: the derived-to-underived comparison on the chosen resolution is the identity.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change), construction immediately before the lemma, with the identity K-flat resolution

proof.text:
Use the balanced tensor relations and pure-tensor generation of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Multiplication is $A$-bilinear and so gives $\mu:B\otimes_A B	o B$. Define $
u:B	o B\otimes_A B$ by $
u(c)=1\otimes c$; both maps are $B$-linear for the second-factor action. We have $\mu
u(c)=c$. For a pure tensor $b\otimes c$, choose $a\in A$ with $f(a)=b$, using surjectivity. Then $b\otimes c=(a\cdot1)\otimes c=1\otimes(a\cdot c)=1\otimes bc=
u\mu(b\otimes c)$. Generation by pure tensors gives $
u\mu=\mathrm{id}$. Hence $\mu$ is an isomorphism with the displayed inverse.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property and balanced tensor relations; explicit surjection calculation

proof.text: The inverse maps in Step 3 give inverse chain maps $\mu[0]$ and $\nu[0]$. The localization functor defining the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] preserves their two inverse equations. Consequently $\mu[0]$ is invertible in $D(B)$; Step 2 identifies this very morphism with the canonical multiplication $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\to B[0]$. It is therefore an isomorphism, also after restriction to $D(A)$.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change), K-flat model; concluding inverse equations
